title: How ai will win everyone out
author: crumbaker
selftext:
Simply put, endless content for many games. I'm surprised I haven't seen this brought up more. For my game that's going to be less than $10 I plan on making free content and dirt cheap expansions for years from now, potentially even offering whole new ways to play the game with all sorts of mods. With traditional methods you would need a studio to do that, and all of the associated costs and time. 

I know we all hate dealing with the anti crowd but they're shrinking everyday ai gets better, especially now with it getting console games to work on pc. With the place ai is in right now, you only limit is your imagination. Amazing time to be alive. Wishlist Stompworks right now: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5383780/Stompworks/?beta=0](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5383780/Stompworks/?beta=0)

replies.author: crumbaker
replies.body: I had to do my plug, but I wanted to get some thoughts on this. I guess there's not much to say other than I'm obviously right about the subject.

comments.author: Rcraft
comments.body:
How much traction have you gotten so far on your wishlist? It seems like a promising game concept. 

Problem with your thesis is that there is still more demand for *truly* good content than there is supply, and I don't see the supply actually getting better. The deluge of AI slop is not significantly nudging the quality bar higher. I could spend a lot more money on games if I felt there were some out there that would surpass the quality of what I have now and AI has not accelerated that. That said, AI could become the lead "best idea generator" and then human developers or designers aren't even involved. Not sure who makes money then.

replies.author: rrcecil
replies.body:
I don’t think we’ve seen the actual projects hit steam yet. Anything coherent or with scope still in the oven. I think early-mid next year we’ll see the impressive stuff.

My attempt at a one prompt shot is now on week 4 and I have like 10 milestones (10 being like full release and post launch roadmap) and I’ve been on milestone 3 for like 3 of those 4 weeks.

Scope creep… but I keep seeing what’s posted on here and just like makes me want to keep it in the oven even LONGER. Like the barrier to entry is low right now but I do believe talented people are currently getting in the flow.

replies.author: Rcraft
replies.body: I agree, I am scouring around for the first signs of an impressive AI-native project, just a few promising ones on the Wishlist. A lot of ones that look good still fail to come together though, for one reason or another. I expect a few to succeed!

comments.author: DoSomeStrangeThings
comments.body:
Majority of players don't want "endless" content. They want a polished one. One good game worth significantly more than years of slop. 

Moreover, you don't need a studio to maintain a game, you need passion and good ideas. Dwarf fortress exists for almost as long as I walk this god forsaken planet, rimworld, stardew. We're developed by a single devs until they truly became popular.

And your game is not it chief. Generic claude UI, barely passable animations (see walking) and special effects, AI generated marketing pitch. Maybe if you get at least current scope of the game to something worth spending time and money, you will understand why no one does "infinite content for dirt cheap"
